items.summary: Decision Transformer (DT) has demonstrated strong performance in various offline reinforcement learning (RL) tasks by conditioning action generation on expected future returns and historical trajectories. However, treating expected future returns as the condition provides an incomplete description of the future, as trajectories with different state transitions and behaviors may share similar returns. Moreover, expected future returns inherently depend on task-specific reward functions, which makes policy learning reliant on reward-labeled datasets and restricts its scalability to tasks with similar but unseen rewards. Recently, Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) have emerged as a promising paradigm of self-supervised learning-based world models, which learn predictive representations of future dynamics in latent space rather than reconstructing future states in the original space. Inspired by JEPA, we propose DT-JEPA, an offline pretraining and online fine-tuning framework that learns general knowledge from reward-free offline trajectories and achieves excellent adaptation to unseen tasks. Instead of predicting a single deterministic future embedding, we design a novel probabilistic predictor to model the conditional distribution of future representations in the latent space, thereby capturing both predictive information and uncertainty about future dynamics. Theoretically, we show that 1) the JEPA objective seeks to maximize a variational lower bound on the mutual information between historical representations and future trajectories; and 2) predictive future-conditioned policy learning admits a finite-sample performance bound with an O(N-1/4) estimation term. Experiments on D4RL benchmarks demonstrate that DT-JEPA achieves efficient adaptation across varying offline RL tasks, outperforming traditional DT-based and other offline RL methods.
items.title: DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making

items.summary: Video provides a natural source of supervision: what happens next serves as a learning signal for visual world modeling. Yet masked video pretraining focuses on recovering missing content from surrounding context rather than predicting the future from the past. Autoregressive methods instead predict forward one token at a time, but have yet to match joint-embedding methods in representation quality. This gap motivates us to revisit the granularity and space of future prediction. In this work, we introduce VANE, a self-supervised visual pretraining framework built on next-frame prediction in embedding space. A causal encoder summarizes past observations for a state predictor that infers the representation of the entire next frame, making temporal evolution the primary learning signal. This prediction is carried out in a fixed embedding space provided by a frozen semantic tokenizer, emphasizing scene content and structure. To retain fine-grained spatial detail alongside semantic content, a lightweight auxiliary generative decoder reconstructs future-frame patches conditioned on the predicted representations. To unify visual modeling across images and videos, we construct a local-to-global crop sequence for still images, allowing the same encoder to predict newly revealed regions from earlier crops under the same objective. Experiments show that VANE improves with model and data scaling, achieving SOTA on most anticipation, recognition, and dense perception benchmarks among unified encoders. Especially on EPIC-KITCHENS-100 action anticipation, it surpasses V-JEPA 2.1 by 7.1 points in mean-class recall@5. These results demonstrate that next-frame prediction in embedding space is effective and scalable for visual world modeling.
items.title: Learning from Next-Frame Prediction: Towards Unified and Scalable Visual World Modeling

items.summary: Unrecognized anomalies in critical infrastructure can rapidly cascade into catastrophic physical or operational failures. Current anomaly detection approaches often rely on direct access to the monitored system by utilizing onboard sensors, such as motor encoders, to detect anomalous states. However, legacy hardware often lacks these sensors, or strict security protocols may prohibit access altogether. We therefore present AWARE, a world model framework that is capable of anomaly detection using only external camera monitoring via system dynamics estimation and state prediction. Evaluated across 240 real-world robotic crane trajectories, including payload collisions and motor degradations, AWARE demonstrates a 26% improvement in anomaly classification over our strongest baseline under noisy, camera-only state estimation. Furthermore, the inferred dynamics parameter can be decoded to identify the source of faults, localizing the degrading motor with 88% accuracy.
items.title: Adaptive World-Models for Anomaly Recognition (AWARE): A Framework for Robot Dynamics Prediction and Introspection

items.summary: Replay-based Continual Learning mitigates catastrophic forgetting by keeping a buffer of past samples, making buffer composition critical under a fixed memory budget. Recent coreset-based replay methods improve buffer quality using model-derived gradients, losses, or auxiliary optimization, but incur substantial computational overhead as memory is repeatedly updated. We propose CARES, a continual model-optimization-free approach for buffer construction that instead exploits the geometry of a frozen pretrained feature space using class-aware, density-weighted coverage. We evaluate CARES across balanced, imbalanced, and label-noisy streams under online class- and task-incremental settings. On Tiny-ImageNet, CARES is 2.3 to 8.8 times faster than existing coreset-based selectors. Although CARES achieves this speedup using no training signal from the continual learner, it ranks among the state of the art across balanced, imbalanced, and label-noisy streams under online class- and task-incremental settings, outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 7.58 percentage points under class imbalance while also attaining higher average accuracy on Tiny-ImageNet. Code will be released upon publication
items.title: CARES: Coverage-Aware Replay Exemplar Selection for Continual Learning

items.summary: Modern vision encoders are widely used as semantic representations, but the relationship between embedding similarity and human-visible semantics can become unclear far from the natural-image manifold. We probe this regime in a black-box setting by applying sparse pixel edits to blank canvases with a simple pixel-level hill-climbing procedure. Across ImageNet and Flickr30k, we evaluate whether these edited blank canvases can retrieve chosen targets in multimodal contrastive encoders and self-supervised visual encoders. On OpenCLIP, inputs optimized toward class prompts achieve strong top-1 and top-5 targeted retrieval performance; on DINOv3, inputs optimized toward class prototypes achieve high target alignment and near-top prototype ranks. These results show that sparse edits on otherwise blank, visually non-semantic inputs can enter target semantic basins in both language-aligned and self-supervised visual representation spaces. Our findings identify a shared off-manifold failure mode of modern vision encoders and suggest sparse blank-canvas optimization as a simple probe of representation geometry.
items.title: SPOOK: Sparse Pixel Optimization for Off-Manifold Knowledge in Vision Encoders

items.summary: Human observers can encounter representations of the same relational contribution history yet form different beliefs about its significance and trustworthiness. This third paper in a coordinated research programme investigates cognitive processes between the structural availability of evidence and an observer’s assessment of a person, claim, or contribution. Its proposed analytic objects are selective attention, evidence encoding, reconstructive memory, attribution, interpretive schemas, belief revision, epistemic vigilance, and behavioral reliance. The inquiry distinguishes evidentiary accessibility from cognitive encounter, subjective confidence from justified assessment, and expressed trust from risk-bearing cooperation. Prior work in attention, working memory, judgment under uncertainty, epistemic vigilance, and trust in automation motivates a provisional sequential-kernel architecture; that architecture remains a research proposal rather than a validated general cognitive model. AI-mediated information environments supply a historically relevant application, without defining the paper’s full scope. This working draft contains all ten planned sections, covering cognitive interfaces, selective attention, memory-based trajectory reconstruction, contribution attribution, proposition-specific belief revision, testimony evaluation, behavioral reliance, empirical designs with explicit identification boundaries, and a synthesis of conditional theoretical findings. It reports no original empirical results.
items.title: Cognitive Mediation of Relational Evidence: An Investigation of Epistemic Judgment and Reliance

items.summary: People differ in how they perceive music, what associations they make with it, what they like about it, and how they respond to it. Computational models intended to simulate people in environments that include music should account for these differences. Although LLMs have been shown to reproduce aspects of human behavior, whether audio-language models (ALMs) can reproduce a specific person's responses to textual and musical stimuli remains underexplored. We introduce MusicTwins, a framework that combines persona summaries, personal memory, and post-training to generate person-specific responses. We construct persona representations from human writings, capturing background, views, personality, writing style, and a musical profile, and post-train Audio Flamingo Next through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Evaluation on ten held-out personas shows notable improvements for Audio Flamingo Next in persona fidelity, including personality, writing style, and responses to music, supporting MusicTwins as a foundation for training audio-language models to listen like their persona.
items.title: MusicTwins: Training Audio-Language Models to Listen like Their Persona

items.summary: Continual Wi-Fi sensing must balance plasticity, learning new rooms or users, against stability, keeping earlier ones, yet nodes often cannot retain channel state information (CSI) for privacy and storage reasons. We propose WiMoT (Wi-Fi Moment Transport), which stores the per-class feature mean and covariance of every earlier domain instead of samples. When the representation changes, stored statistics become stale. WiMoT restricts the change to an affine map on a frozen feature basis and applies the same map to the statistics, so they stay valid without old samples. Supervised contrastive learning learns the new domain, a closed-form loss on the stored statistics keeps earlier classes separable, and a Gaussian discriminant classifier, refitted from the transported statistics with equal weight per domain, predicts without domain identity. On 3DO, WiMANS, and Widar3.0, WiMoT's average final accuracies are 94.02%, 89.61%, and 95.16% with at most 0.58 percentage points (pp) of forgetting. On 3DO and Widar3.0, it also has the highest balance of new- and earlier-domain accuracy and is 3.77 and 13.11 pp ahead of the strongest of 21 baselines, which uses replay, staying ahead across domain orders and label budgets. On WiMANS, it matches the strongest replay baseline in accuracy (+0.41 pp) while reducing forgetting from 2.78 to 0.00 pp, and has the highest six-order average accuracy. Because full covariances dominate the memory, storing them as rank-32 factors shrinks the moment memory to 6.4%, losing at most 0.49 pp of accuracy, within edge-node storage budgets.
items.title: WiMoT: Replay-Free Continual Wi-Fi Sensing via Moment Transport

items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models reduce computation through sparse activation, but storing their expert parameters remains a major memory bottleneck. We introduce GS-MoE, a training-free compression framework that addresses redundancy across and within experts through two compression axes: shared-subspace rank and expert intermediate width. Groupwise low-rank representations capture shared structure across experts while retaining expert-specific projections, and Nyström-based neuron compression reduces intermediate width within each expert. For fixed shared subspaces, we derive per-expert reconstruction-error reductions from the reconstruction objective and use them to guide expert grouping. Budgets are allocated hierarchically using a gradient-free layer-importance score to guide the allocation of rank and width budgets across layers, which eigenvalues and leverage then distribute as non-uniform ranks across groups and intermediate widths across experts. Experiments demonstrate the complementary benefits of compression along both axes, particularly at high compression rates on fine-grained MoE models. On DeepSeek-MoE-16B-Base, at a 60% reduction in total model parameters, GS-MoE retains approximately 90% of the uncompressed model's average reasoning performance, compared with 73% for D$^2$-MoE, while achieving 20% lower out-of-domain perplexity. We provide a code implementation at: https://github.com/cbacary/GS-MoE
items.title: GS-MoE: Training-Free MoE Compression via Groupwise Subspace Sharing and Pruning

items.summary: Humans efficiently process multimodal streams spanning hours to years, building persistent, fine-grained spatiotemporal memories that support reasoning about and predicting long-horizon events. In contrast, existing benchmarks focus on short- and medium-context tasks, and most foundation models struggle to preserve fine-grained information over long horizons. To evaluate and improve long-horizon spatiotemporal reasoning, we introduce the LongVideo dataset and the 4DMemoryBench. LongVideo comprises about 900 hours of video and over 5,000 manually reviewed questions covering visual, textual, and spatiotemporal reasoning across diverse context lengths. We further develop the 4DMemory Harness, which integrates four complementary skills, 22+ specialized tool models, and a model-specific retrieval-augmented generation system. Evaluating 13 leading models, we find that standalone foundation models struggle with long-horizon tasks, while the 4DMemory Harness improves all of them by over 50\%. Compared to previous benchmark, the same models exhibit a performance drop of more than 10\% on 4DMemoryBench. We hope 4DMemory will facilitate the development of spatiotemporal agents capable of addressing complex, long-horizon tasks.
items.title: 4DMemory: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Spatiotemporal Memory with Harness-Augmented Agents

items.summary: Enterprises are deploying agentic AI across the software development lifecycle, and they need the behavioral logic of the systems they act on, not stakeholder documentation. A seven-agent reverse-engineering pipeline recovered this logic, processing 241 repositories across 18 services into thousands of artifacts describing scope, journeys, rules and acceptance criteria. Recovery does not confer usability. Entities like offer, eligibility, and activation recur across services under a shared vocabulary, related in name but operationally distinct, so one end-to-end journey implicates over a thousand near-identical rules that must not be conflated. Flat vector retrieval fails, returning an identical rule from the wrong service at high similarity with no signal of error. Content-level ontology, the traditional remedy, did not exist, and relating every occurrence of recurring entities would have cost more than the engagement and not survived a release cycle. We place the ontology at the artifact level. In this machine-generated corpus, each artifact retains its producer, component, service, domain and type, provenance that disambiguates before content is read. We present a knowledge layer that organizes before retrieving: a self-describing catalog, a sparse metadata registry, and a navigation hypergraph defined over artifacts rather than extracted entities. Queries resolve to artifact identifiers that constrain vector search, so the competing rule from another service is absent rather than outranked, making disambiguation structural, not statistical. Built in under a week and admitting new services by convention, the layer serves SDLC agents, developers, quality engineers and analysts. It supported root-cause analysis and resolution of 100+ production defects with developer verification and attributed 35 release regression failures to specific rules and services.
items.title: Reimagining Enterprise RAG for Multi-Agent Systems: A Knowledge Layer That Organizes Before It Retrieves

items.summary: Deepwave provides wave propagation modules for PyTorch, for applications such as seismic imaging and inversion. It performs forward modelling and backpropagation, so it can simulate wave propagation to generate synthetic data, or invert for the scattering potential (reverse-time migration, RTM, or its least-squares counterpart, LSRTM), other model parameters (full-waveform inversion, FWI), initial wavefields, or source wavelets. It can also be used inside a larger chain of operations, with forward and backpropagation flowing through the whole chain end to end. You can use your own objective functions, or functions that generate the propagator's inputs, and PyTorch's automatic differentiation calculates how to backpropagate through them. New to seismic/wave-equation terminology? The glossary defines the terms (PML, CFL, Born, FWI, and more) used throughout this README and the rest of the documentation. Deepwave requires Python 3.9 or later and PyTorch 2.4 or later. First install PyTorch for your CPU or CUDA device using the instructions on the PyTorch website . Then install Deepwave: pip install deepwave   macOS wheels support Apple Silicon. Intel Mac wheels are no longer provided: PyTorch 2.4 and newer do not publish wheels for that platform. Prebuilt x86 wheels require AVX2. Older CPUs need a source build; see installation troubleshooting . PyTorch is Deepwave's only dependency. The example scripts under docs/ additionally import matplotlib (to draw their figures) and, in some cases, numpy , scipy (smoothing and filter design), torchaudio (applying those filters), torchvision and geomloss , but those are needed only to run the examples, never by Deepwave itself. To install all of them: pip install 'deepwave[examples]'   The documentation contains examples and instructions on how to install and use Deepwave. You might also like to watch a video summary of Deepwave . Not every propagator supports every option (dimensionality, backend, boundary faces, batching, second-order differentiation, callbacks, ...). See the capability matrix (declared in the code and checked by conformance tests) before assuming a combination works. Why Deepwave Computationally efficient. Deepwave's compiled kernels use a hand-derived adjoint for better performance and lower memory requirements than pure PyTorch implementations. See what Deepwave calculates . Second derivatives are supported, not just first. The scalar, acoustic, and elastic propagators can compute Hessian-vector products (derivatives of gradients); see the Hessian example . Born (linearised) modelling. Model scattered waves from perturbations to a background medium for linearised inversion and imaging. See the torch.func example . Deepwave fits into an ordinary PyTorch workflow. Because propagation is a normal PyTorch autograd Function , it works directly with PyTorch optimisers, DistributedDataParallel over shots, torch.func transforms, and any PyTorch loss function or neural-network model of the input parameters. See the capability matrix for exactly what each propagator supports. Deepwave does not try to be a general symbolic PDE solver, a multi-node HPC code, or a non-differentiable simulation toolkit — see Devito , SPECFEM , and k-Wave respectively for those needs. If you are choosing between wave-propagation packages, see the comparison guide . (Note: the DeepWave-KAUST GitHub organisation, home of the SWEEP package, is unrelated to this project.) Features Supports the 1D, 2D, and 3D constant density acoustic / scalar wave equation (regular and Born modelling), variable density acoustic, elastic, viscoacoustic (single-mechanism SLS attenuation), elastic VTI (anisotropic), and pseudo-acoustic VTI ( deepwave.acoustic_vti , the Duveneck et al. 2008 V_S=0 reduction) wave equations Runs on CPUs and appropriate GPUs The gradient of all outputs (final wavefields and receiver data) can be calculated with respect to the model parameters (wavespeed, scattering potential, etc
items.title: Deepwave

items.summary: We conduct a version-pinned, reproducible forensic audit of the public Einstein Elevator data package (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.15167723) to determine whether it supports validation of quantum sensor certificates. Through an exhaustive cross-file sliding-window correlation search over 44,207,922 comparisons and exact six-decimal rounding checks, we find that all 31 exported sensor channels have a unique best match within the enumerated raw traces under the stated protocol. Residual numerical differences are highly consistent with text-based absolute quantization; the correlation-loss approximation 1 - r ≈ δ² / (24σx²) is diagnostic for this dataset, not a universal proof. We inspect the MATLAB-derived 318-point population series and reconcile it with a 2022 workbook entry only at the level of counts. An archive-wide search of 181 file objects and 1,654 MATLAB metadata fields finds no documented join key linking the 2022 run-indexed population series to the 2017 timestamped traces under the enumerated search protocol. Using Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds and a Charnes-Cooper linearization, we establish that the public archive does not supply the joint observations needed to identify the EKF false-safe risk without additional coupling assumptions; the formal program is illustrative and is not populated with empirical failure/acceptance coefficients because the required linked observations are absent. We frame this as a bounded data-contract limitation for downstream statistical validation, not as a failure of the original experiment.
items.title: A Reproducible Provenance Audit of the Public Einstein Elevator Data Package: Trace Correspondence, Metadata Linkage, and the Non-Identifiability of Sensor-Certificate Risk from the Public Archive

items.summary: PGA-G v1.0.0 — Research Software and Experimental Evidence This release provides the original research implementation and reproducibility resources for PGA-G: Selective Adaptation and Conformal Calibration for Speech Deepfake Detection . PGA-G introduces a selective adaptation framework that determines when a frozen speech deepfake detector should be adapted using unlabelled deployment data and a genuine-speech reference. The proposed methodology integrates prevalence-based adaptation gating, consistency screening, and conformal calibration to support reliable operating decisions under changing deployment conditions. Research Contributions Selective adaptation: A prevalence-based gate determines whether the deployment data provide sufficient evidence to consider adaptation. Consistency screening: A guard evaluates the adapted scoring branch to reduce reference-dependent shortcuts. Conformal calibration: A genuine-reference calibration procedure establishes operating points under the specified calibration assumptions. Cross-detector evaluation: Experiments examine SSL-AASIST, XLSR-Mamba, and AASIST on ASVspoof 2021 DF and ASVspoof 5. Release Contents The repository includes the research implementation, pre-registered experimental protocols, per-repetition evaluation records, machine-readable numerical results, provenance information, automated tests, and reproducibility documentation. Reproducibility and Verification The included verification framework supports independent examination of the archived experimental evidence, including: 160/160 confirmatory numerical comparisons. 20/20 additional numerical consistency checks. Byte-identical regeneration of the source-grouped numerical summary. Automated file-integrity validation and regression testing. Reconstruction of condition-level experimental evidence from archived results. These checks run without requiring GPU access, pretrained model checkpoints, or original speech recordings. Full detector inference and complete experimental repetition require separately obtained upstream resources and additional environment-specific setup, as documented in the repository. Research Artifact Scope This release serves as a companion research software and experimental evidence archive. It does not distribute the journal manuscript, publication figures, original speech recordings, or third-party pretrained model weights. The repository provides an independently inspectable foundation for evaluating the PGA-G methodology and its reported experimental findings.
items.title: PGA-G: Selective Adaptation and Conformal Calibration for Speech Deepfake Detection

items.summary: Inferring constitutive laws from transient response data is a central inverse problem in soft condensed-matter physics, particularly when the relevant relaxation spectrum extends beyond the time window of a single experiment. Time-temperature superposition (TTS) constrains this problem for thermorheologically simple materials in the linear viscoelastic regime by allowing temperature to rescale the characteristic relaxation time without changing the underlying shape of the relaxation spectrum. We incorporate this constraint into a physics-informed machine-learning framework for time-resolved mechanical spectroscopy via chirp rheometry. We encode compact fractional viscoelastic models as causal convolutional features derived from the Boltzmann superposition principle, and we jointly fit multi-temperature chirp records using sparse variational Gaussian process regression. The model infers horizontal shift factors, constitutive parameters, and an observational-noise scale directly from time-domain stress-strain signals measured in the linear viscoelastic regime, without first extracting frequency-domain spectra or manually shifting separate curves. For synthetic Fractional Maxwell data, the method recovers the generating constitutive law from a prescribed model library and latent shifts over stress-noise levels from 3% to 25%. Applied to a DGEBA-IPDA epoxy dataset spanning the glass-transition regime, the pooled likelihood distinguishes competing fractional rheology models using the Bayesian information criterion. These results recast TTS master-curve construction as probabilistic inference over latent time rescaling and linear viscoelasticity, while also identifying limitations, such as homoscedastic noise and weakly informative spectral regimes.
items.title: Time-temperature superposition from multi-temperature chirp rheometry of thermorheologically simple materials via physics-informed Gaussian processes

items.summary: We consider the small-time asymptotic expansions for the Dirichlet and Open heat contents of convex planar domains. We prove that the small-time asymptotic expansion for the Open heat content can determine a triangle among triangles, a parallelogram among parallelograms, and an acute trapezium among acute trapezia of the same height. In addition, for a sequence of convex polygons converging to a convex set with smooth boundary in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ in the small-time asymptotic expansions of the Dirichlet and the Open heat contents converge to those of the limiting set. While, for a sequence of convex sets with smooth boundary converging to a convex polygon in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ do not converge to that of the limiting polygon.
items.title: Inverse problems and continuity of heat content coefficients

Its proposed analytic objects are selective attention, evidence encoding, reconstructive memory, attribution, interpretive schemas, belief revision, epistemic vigilance, and behavioral reliance. The inquiry distinguishes evidentiary accessibility from cognitive encounter, subjective confidence from justified assessment, and expressed trust from risk-bearing cooperation. Prior work in attention, working memory, judgment under uncertainty, epistemic vigilance, and trust in automation motivates a provisional sequential-kernel architecture; that architecture remains a research proposal rather than a validated general cognitive model. AI-mediated information environments supply a historically relevant application, without defining the paper’s full scope. This working draft contains all ten planned sections, covering cognitive interfaces, selective attention, memory-based trajectory reconstruction, contribution attribution, proposition-specific belief revision, testimony evaluation, behavioral reliance, empirical designs with explicit identification boundaries, and a synthesis of conditional theoretical findings. It reports no original empirical results.
items.title: Cognitive Mediation of Relational Evidence: An Investigation of Epistemic Judgment and Reliance

items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models reduce computation through sparse activation, but storing their expert parameters remains a major memory bottleneck. We introduce GS-MoE, a training-free compression framework that addresses redundancy across and within experts through two compression axes: shared-subspace rank and expert intermediate width. Groupwise low-rank representations capture shared structure across experts while retaining expert-specific projections, and Nyström-based neuron compression reduces intermediate width within each expert. For fixed shared subspaces, we derive per-expert reconstruction-error reductions from the reconstruction objective and use them to guide expert grouping. Budgets are allocated hierarchically using a gradient-free layer-importance score to guide the allocation of rank and width budgets across layers, which eigenvalues and leverage then distribute as non-uniform ranks across groups and intermediate widths across experts. Experiments demonstrate the complementary benefits of compression along both axes, particularly at high compression rates on fine-grained MoE models. On DeepSeek-MoE-16B-Base, at a 60% reduction in total model parameters, GS-MoE retains approximately 90% of the uncompressed model's average reasoning performance, compared with 73% for D$^2$-MoE, while achieving 20% lower out-of-domain perplexity. We provide a code implementation at: https://github.com/cbacary/GS-MoE
items.title: GS-MoE: Training-Free MoE Compression via Groupwise Subspace Sharing and Pruning

items.summary: Bidirectional (right-to-left, RTL) layout defects arise when interfaces authored with physical directional CSS (margin-left, border-left, text-align:left) are rendered under dir="rtl" without being mirrored. Accessibility engines (axe-core), actionability engines (Playwright), and even Stylelint's current core logical-property rule fail to localise these defects. We present runtime structural invariants -- a zero-golden mode over computed style and geometry, and a bidi-conservative differential mode -- that catch them in a headless browser. On a held-out benchmark of 14 real RTL bugs reconstructed from dated fix commits in Bootstrap and Material Components Web, the detector recovers 13/14 (2 via zero-golden, 11 via the differential mode), with no false alarm on any patched version; on the actual committed historical bootstrap.rtl.css it catches 1 of 2 attempted. It reports 0 false positives on 16 negative LTR-island cases and, in both modes, on 43 unmodified real components across four design systems and three RTL architectures (rule-of-three 95% upper bound <= 7%), and it surfaced a real directional defect in the current Bulma 1.0.4. By contrast, Stylelint's core rule emits an identical 1744 warnings on Bootstrap's LTR and correct-RTL builds, pseudo-localisation detects none of the mirroring bugs, and a naive pixel mirror-and-diff reaches only F1 0.87 with a test-set-tuned threshold. The two modes are complementary: zero-golden is the sole detector of the decoration/styling-asymmetry class (5/6) but false-flags the correct logical border-inline-end, while the differential detects none of that class yet never false-alarms and is empirically exact on the block-level inset/margin class. We scope this paper to detection; repair is future work.
items.title: Runtime BiDi Structural Verification Catches Right-to-Left Layout Defects that Accessibility, Actionability, and Logical-Property Linting Miss

items.summary: We conduct a version-pinned, reproducible forensic audit of the public Einstein Elevator data package (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.15167723) to determine whether it supports validation of quantum sensor certificates. Through an exhaustive cross-file sliding-window correlation search over 44,207,922 comparisons and exact six-decimal rounding checks, we find that all 31 exported sensor channels have a unique best match within the enumerated raw traces under the stated protocol. Residual numerical differences are highly consistent with text-based absolute quantization; the correlation-loss approximation 1 - r ≈ δ² / (24σx²) is diagnostic for this dataset, not a universal proof. We inspect the MATLAB-derived 318-point population series and reconcile it with a 2022 workbook entry only at the level of counts. An archive-wide search of 181 file objects and 1,654 MATLAB metadata fields finds no documented join key linking the 2022 run-indexed population series to the 2017 timestamped traces under the enumerated search protocol. Using Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds and a Charnes-Cooper linearization, we establish that the public archive does not supply the joint observations needed to identify the EKF false-safe risk without additional coupling assumptions; the formal program is illustrative and is not populated with empirical failure/acceptance coefficients because the required linked observations are absent. items.title: A Reproducible Provenance Audit of the Public Einstein Elevator Data Package: Trace Correspondence, Metadata Linkage, and the Non-Identifiability of Sensor-Certificate Risk from the Public Archive

items.summary: Bulk transcriptomic differences between groups reflect both altered cell composition and altered expression within cells. Methods such as csSAM, TOAST and CIBERSORTx separate the two, but all require additional information: measured per-sample proportions, anchor genes, or an external reference. We examine what can be established under a pure-bulk paired design in which none of this information is available. We formalise the decomposition obs = comp + resid and test three propositions: whether resid can be interpreted as within-cell regulation; how closely comp tracks obs, and what that agreement depends on; and whether the number of cell compartments is a well-defined model-complexity variable. Data comprise four abdominal aortic aneurysm cohorts, one lung cohort and the HLCA normal lung atlas (584,944 cells × 27,402 genes). Deconvolution uses a self-implemented Lawson–Hanson non-negative least squares validated on three problems with known answers. comp + resid = obs is an algebraic identity (same-source R² = 1.000000000000000). resid cannot be interpreted as within-cell regulation: apart from a degenerate case, the control cell-type-specific profile is not point-identifiable, and swapping reference profiles in a zero-regulation construction drives resid to −5.4654. Pearson r between comp and obs is 0.7335 (0.7001–0.8041) under platform-matched pseudo-bulk conditions, 0.2379–0.3791 across four aorta cohorts, and 0.1675–0.3019 for lung UIP/IPF; regression slopes are 0.078–0.801. A fully crossed 3 × 3 design with four aggregation weights shows that with six reference compartments r ranges from 0.2674 to 0.8417 (SD 0.239) and is not identifiable. comp is an approximate index of compositional change; resid carries no inferable information about within-cell regulation; and the number of compartments is not a well-defined model-complexity variable. --- 群体间 bulk 转录组差异同时反映细胞组成的改变与细胞内表达的改变。csSAM、TOAST、CIBERSORTx 等方法可将两者分开,但都需要额外信息:测得的逐样本比例、锚定基因,或外部参考。本文考察在上述信息全部不可得的纯 bulk 配对设计下,这一归因能做到什么程度、边界在哪里。我们形式化分解 obs = comp + resid,并检验三个命题:resid 能否解释为细胞内调控;comp 与 obs 的一致性能达到多少、依赖什么;以及「细胞区室数」是否为良定义的模型复杂度变量。数据包括四个腹主动脉瘤队列、一个肺队列,以及 HLCA 正常肺图谱(584,944 细胞 × 27,402 基因)。解卷积用自实现的 Lawson–Hanson 非负最小二乘,在三个已知答案问题上验证。comp + resid = obs 是代数恒等式(同源 R² = 1.000000000000000)。resid 不能解释为细胞内调控:除退化情形外,对照组细胞类型特异谱不可点识别;在零调控构造中对调参考谱可使 resid 达到 −5.4654。comp 与 obs 的 Pearson r:平台匹配伪 bulk 为 0.7335(0.7001–0.8041);主动脉四队列 0.2379–0.3791;肺 UIP/IPF 0.1675–0.3019。回归斜率 0.078–0.801。完全交叉的 3 × 3 设计配合四种聚合权重显示:参考区室数为 6 时 r 在 0.2674–0.8417 间摆动(SD 0.239),不可识别。comp 可作为组成变化的近似指标;resid 不承载可推断的细胞内调控信息;区室数不是良定义的模型复杂度变量。 --- This record contains the English and the Chinese version of the manuscript, both as PDF and as editable source, together with the companion manuscript on six failure modes (files 03 and 04). items.summary: Enterprises are deploying agentic AI across the software development lifecycle, and they need the behavioral logic of the systems they act on, not stakeholder documentation. A seven-agent reverse-engineering pipeline recovered this logic, processing 241 repositories across 18 services into thousands of artifacts describing scope, journeys, rules and acceptance criteria. Recovery does not confer usability. Entities like offer, eligibility, and activation recur across services under a shared vocabulary, related in name but operationally distinct, so one end-to-end journey implicates over a thousand near-identical rules that must not be conflated. Flat vector retrieval fails, returning an identical rule from the wrong service at high similarity with no signal of error. Content-level ontology, the traditional remedy, did not exist, and relating every occurrence of recurring entities would have cost more than the engagement and not survived a release cycle. We place the ontology at the artifact level. In this machine-generated corpus, each artifact retains its producer, component, service, domain and type, provenance that disambiguates before content is read. We present a knowledge layer that organizes before retrieving: a self-describing catalog, a sparse metadata registry, and a navigation hypergraph defined over artifacts rather than extracted entities. Queries resolve to artifact identifiers that constrain vector search, so the competing rule from another service is absent rather than outranked, making disambiguation structural, not statistical. Built in under a week and admitting new services by convention, the layer serves SDLC agents, developers, quality engineers and analysts. It supported root-cause analysis and resolution of 100+ production defects with developer verification and attributed 35 release regression failures to specific rules and services.
items.title: Reimagining Enterprise RAG for Multi-Agent Systems: A Knowledge Layer That Organizes Before It Retrieves

items.summary: Unrecognized anomalies in critical infrastructure can rapidly cascade into catastrophic physical or operational failures. Current anomaly detection approaches often rely on direct access to the monitored system by utilizing onboard sensors, such as motor encoders, to detect anomalous states. However, legacy hardware often lacks these sensors, or strict security protocols may prohibit access altogether. We therefore present AWARE, a world model framework that is capable of anomaly detection using only external camera monitoring via system dynamics estimation and state prediction. Evaluated across 240 real-world robotic crane trajectories, including payload collisions and motor degradations, AWARE demonstrates a 26% improvement in anomaly classification over our strongest baseline under noisy, camera-only state estimation. Furthermore, the inferred dynamics parameter can be decoded to identify the source of faults, localizing the degrading motor with 88% accuracy.
items.title: Adaptive World-Models for Anomaly Recognition (AWARE): A Framework for Robot Dynamics Prediction and Introspection

items.summary: Modern vision encoders are widely used as semantic representations, but the relationship between embedding similarity and human-visible semantics can become unclear far from the natural-image manifold. We probe this regime in a black-box setting by applying sparse pixel edits to blank canvases with a simple pixel-level hill-climbing procedure. Across ImageNet and Flickr30k, we evaluate whether these edited blank canvases can retrieve chosen targets in multimodal contrastive encoders and self-supervised visual encoders. On OpenCLIP, inputs optimized toward class prompts achieve strong top-1 and top-5 targeted retrieval performance; on DINOv3, inputs optimized toward class prototypes achieve high target alignment and near-top prototype ranks. These results show that sparse edits on otherwise blank, visually non-semantic inputs can enter target semantic basins in both language-aligned and self-supervised visual representation spaces. Our findings identify a shared off-manifold failure mode of modern vision encoders and suggest sparse blank-canvas optimization as a simple probe of representation geometry.
items.title: SPOOK: Sparse Pixel Optimization for Off-Manifold Knowledge in Vision Encoders

items.summary: Nine years after its introduction, the transformer remains the default sequence model. The usual explanations are real: parallel matrix multiplication on accelerators, predictable returns to scale, a co-evolved ecosystem and exact recall from an uncompressed context. But they do not explain why most modifications barely move accuracy, which properties are essential, why the changes practice adopted took the forms they did, or where the design can still move. This paper is the entry point to a collection of papers that treat a token-mixing layer as an averaging operator rebuilt from its own input and iterated through depth. Such a layer faces six failure modes (collapse to consensus, contamination of content by routing, runaway feedback, the inability to abstain, dilution as context grows, and the inability to represent direction). Each has a protection, proved within a declared class, and a signature measured at small scale when that protection is removed; for gain control, which protects against runaway feedback, that signature is synthetic. We read softmax attention in a pre-normalized residual block as the one known point where all six protections are cheap at once under the prices of parallel hardware and gradient descent; this is an interpretation, not a measured optimum. Two mechanisms, measured at small scale, help explain why its neighbourhood is flat: trained networks compensate local deficits through spare capacity, and, in ten scored tests, making a protection explicit did not beat a block that already supplies it. The anchor, the residual or input path that protects against collapse to consensus, is the one protection whose loss compensation provably cannot repair: under strict mixing, where repeated averaging contracts token differences toward zero, no extra capacity of bounded gain (bounded sensitivity) brings back what is lost without it, and in small-model ablations nothing else in the block made up for it. This is a proved bound; a trained test that adds capacity is pending. Many changes adopted in the mixing layer and its block since 2017, among them pre-normalization, QK-norm, sinks and output gates, read as re-supplies of the same protections; the account is silent on others, such as changes to the MLP. The room that remains for the design to move is where a protection is patched (met only by a fix that works over a limited range, such as the trained length) or paid at a price that another design could avoid. It includes abstention and retrieval at long context, governed by a two-sided log-N law in the context length (with bounded scores, no fixed rule for abstaining keeps both as the context grows), and bounded memory, whose price for exact recall is a per-head capacity. It also includes decisions that sum over all competitors where reading the largest would do, and the writer of new features (in a transformer, the MLP and the output map), for which the collection has no theory yet of what a good writer computes. Along the way the collection establishes results that stand on their own: attention has an arrow that default statistics of a single operator cannot see; depth is a distribution over path lengths; converged adaptive averaging can amplify changes in its input and overturn correct predictions; and softmax obeys length laws that decisions on maxima escape while the competing scores stay below the decision's threshold. We state what is proved, what is measured, what is interpretation, and what is still pending. This is a working draft, not a final version. It is unpolished in places, incomplete in others, and keeps exploratory material a polished paper would leave out, because that material helps decide what comes next and shows the programme's big picture more fully. Please read it with that in mind: the work will be refined further, and later versions will appear under this record. It belongs to a collection released together on Zenodo: the entry paper The Transformer Abides, the monograph A Spectra

items.summary: A sequence-mixing layer that is iterated through depth and rebuilt from its own input faces six failure modes. Each is met by a protection—anchoring, alignment, gain control, abstention, a routing budget, or an arrow—with an operator-level statement proved within a declared class, a signature when it is removed, and a price. We organize attention designs as a lattice of kernel, dynamical, and block constraints in which relaxing a constraint buys a capability and obliges a re-supply. We read softmax attention inside a pre-normalized residual block as the lattice point where every protection is either supplied or cheaply re-supplied under parallel-hardware and optimization pricing: of the deficits tested, all but the anchor's were compensated by capacity elsewhere in the deeper models, and explicit protection knobs did not beat the block, both measured at small scale, while corner structure, by which designs would jump rather than drift, remains a hypothesis. The lattice reads the selected adopted changes to the mixing layer, its normalization and its residual path over the last decade as cheap re-supplies of protections, and it locates the room for change. The clearest room is abstention, governed by a two-sided log-N law: with a bounded logit scale, no null keeps both abstention and single-key retrieval as context grows, and tempering the entire logit budget with log N keeps both when its margins are strictly separated. A controlled pilot follows the law, while a prespecified test of its sink prediction on an open production model was undecided by its prespecified rule; descriptively its slopes leaned toward compensation through position, in which position encoding holds the background's growth down. In a prespecified trained harness of 125M-parameter language models, tempering every logit by log N / log N_train on top of YaRN, which already carries a log-length temperature, did not keep abstention and raised long-context perplexity. In these language models every rule that gives attention a null removed the first-token sink and cut massive activations by 67% to 82%, as earlier reports for gates and attention biases found, and, sigmoid aside, lowered perplexity slightly at the training length; the comparison registered for two of these rules held in every seed, while the same comparison failed in the harness's vision transformers. We close with falsifiable predictions for future architectures, most of them not yet tested. This is a working draft, not a final version. It is unpolished in places, incomplete in others, and keeps exploratory material a polished paper would leave out, because that material helps decide what comes next and shows the programme's big picture more fully. items.summary: Supervised pairwise graph representations convert pairwise predictive relations into sample-specific graphs, but graph-level accuracy does not by itself show that higher-order topology carries the signal. In a controlled Transformer error-detection task, supervised pairwise graphs outperform attention-as-adjacency (ROC-AUC $0.839$ versus $0.559$; the comparable no-confidence pair is $0.687$ versus $0.559$), but their apparent advantage over model confidence disappears after controlling for sequence length, which is almost perfectly recoverable from the pooled hidden state ($R^2=0.9995$). On published HCP Emotion ensemble graphs, signed node aggregation already acts as an ensemble of supervised pairwise predictions. Edge magnitude alone is near chance; topology-aware augmentations change ROC-AUC by at most $0.004$, with only sign-separated degree showing small positive changes across all tested graph sizes, while a validation-tuned three-layer GCN provides no measurable improvement over the signed node-summary baseline. A Fisher post-hoc corrector satisfies its distribution-agnostic guarantees across the evaluated feature representations and remains stable under reduced labelled budgets; in a near-error-free fMRI calibration regime the bound correctly becomes statistically uninformative. A separate cross-attention analysis identifies a redundant reversal circuit and downstream EOS-timing and copy failures. Higher-order topology should therefore be credited only after local supervised evidence and recoverable nuisance variables have been excluded.
items.title: Interpreting Supervised Pairwise Graph Representations: Local Evidence, Confounding, and Provable Post-hoc Correction

items.summary: Inferring constitutive laws from transient response data is a central inverse problem in soft condensed-matter physics, particularly when the relevant relaxation spectrum extends beyond the time window of a single experiment. Time-temperature superposition (TTS) constrains this problem for thermorheologically simple materials in the linear viscoelastic regime by allowing temperature to rescale the characteristic relaxation time without changing the underlying shape of the relaxation spectrum. We incorporate this constraint into a physics-informed machine-learning framework for time-resolved mechanical spectroscopy via chirp rheometry. We encode compact fractional viscoelastic models as causal convolutional features derived from the Boltzmann superposition principle, and we jointly fit multi-temperature chirp records using sparse variational Gaussian process regression. The model infers horizontal shift factors, constitutive parameters, and an observational-noise scale directly from time-domain stress-strain signals measured in the linear viscoelastic regime, without first extracting frequency-domain spectra or manually shifting separate curves. For synthetic Fractional Maxwell data, the method recovers the generating constitutive law from a prescribed model library and latent shifts over stress-noise levels from 3% to 25%. Applied to a DGEBA-IPDA epoxy dataset spanning the glass-transition regime, the pooled likelihood distinguishes competing fractional rheology models using the Bayesian information criterion. These results recast TTS master-curve construction as probabilistic inference over latent time rescaling and linear viscoelasticity, while also identifying limitations, such as homoscedastic noise and weakly informative spectral regimes.
items.title: Time-temperature superposition from multi-temperature chirp rheometry of thermorheologically simple materials via physics-informed Gaussian processes

Accessibility engines (axe-core), actionability engines (Playwright), and even Stylelint's current core logical-property rule fail to localise these defects. We present runtime structural invariants -- a zero-golden mode over computed style and geometry, and a bidi-conservative differential mode -- that catch them in a headless browser. On a held-out benchmark of 14 real RTL bugs reconstructed from dated fix commits in Bootstrap and Material Components Web, the detector recovers 13/14 (2 via zero-golden, 11 via the differential mode), with no false alarm on any patched version; on the actual committed historical bootstrap.rtl.css it catches 1 of 2 attempted. It reports 0 false positives on 16 negative LTR-island cases and, in both modes, on 43 unmodified real components across four design systems and three RTL architectures (rule-of-three 95% upper bound <= 7%), and it surfaced a real directional defect in the current Bulma 1.0.4. By contrast, Stylelint's core rule emits an identical 1744 warnings on Bootstrap's LTR and correct-RTL builds, pseudo-localisation detects none of the mirroring bugs, and a naive pixel mirror-and-diff reaches only F1 0.87 with a test-set-tuned threshold. The two modes are complementary: zero-golden is the sole detector of the decoration/styling-asymmetry class (5/6) but false-flags the correct logical border-inline-end, while the differential detects none of that class yet never false-alarms and is empirically exact on the block-level inset/margin class. We scope this paper to detection; repair is future work.
items.title: Runtime BiDi Structural Verification Catches Right-to-Left Layout Defects that Accessibility, Actionability, and Logical-Property Linting Miss

items.summary: Video provides a natural source of supervision: what happens next serves as a learning signal for visual world modeling. Yet masked video pretraining focuses on recovering missing content from surrounding context rather than predicting the future from the past. Autoregressive methods instead predict forward one token at a time, but have yet to match joint-embedding methods in representation quality. This gap motivates us to revisit the granularity and space of future prediction. In this work, we introduce VANE, a self-supervised visual pretraining framework built on next-frame prediction in embedding space. A causal encoder summarizes past observations for a state predictor that infers the representation of the entire next frame, making temporal evolution the primary learning signal. This prediction is carried out in a fixed embedding space provided by a frozen semantic tokenizer, emphasizing scene content and structure. To retain fine-grained spatial detail alongside semantic content, a lightweight auxiliary generative decoder reconstructs future-frame patches conditioned on the predicted representations. To unify visual modeling across images and videos, we construct a local-to-global crop sequence for still images, allowing the same encoder to predict newly revealed regions from earlier crops under the same objective. Experiments show that VANE improves with model and data scaling, achieving SOTA on most anticipation, recognition, and dense perception benchmarks among unified encoders. Especially on EPIC-KITCHENS-100 action anticipation, it surpasses V-JEPA 2.1 by 7.1 points in mean-class recall@5. These results demonstrate that next-frame prediction in embedding space is effective and scalable for visual world modeling.
items.title: Learning from Next-Frame Prediction: Towards Unified and Scalable Visual World Modeling

items.summary: Decision Transformer (DT) has demonstrated strong performance in various offline reinforcement learning (RL) tasks by conditioning action generation on expected future returns and historical trajectories. However, treating expected future returns as the condition provides an incomplete description of the future, as trajectories with different state transitions and behaviors may share similar returns. Moreover, expected future returns inherently depend on task-specific reward functions, which makes policy learning reliant on reward-labeled datasets and restricts its scalability to tasks with similar but unseen rewards. Recently, Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) have emerged as a promising paradigm of self-supervised learning-based world models, which learn predictive representations of future dynamics in latent space rather than reconstructing future states in the original space. Inspired by JEPA, we propose DT-JEPA, an offline pretraining and online fine-tuning framework that learns general knowledge from reward-free offline trajectories and achieves excellent adaptation to unseen tasks. Instead of predicting a single deterministic future embedding, we design a novel probabilistic predictor to model the conditional distribution of future representations in the latent space, thereby capturing both predictive information and uncertainty about future dynamics. Theoretically, we show that 1) the JEPA objective seeks to maximize a variational lower bound on the mutual information between historical representations and future trajectories; and 2) predictive future-conditioned policy learning admits a finite-sample performance bound with an O(N-1/4) estimation term. Experiments on D4RL benchmarks demonstrate that DT-JEPA achieves efficient adaptation across varying offline RL tasks, outperforming traditional DT-based and other offline RL methods.
items.title: DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making

items.summary: EXTERNAL QIGONG AND HUMAN THERMAL RADIATION PATTERNS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English research working monograph investigating whether thermographic differences observed during culturally defined qigong and matched neutral tasks can be distinguished from ordinary human thermoregulation, environmental exchange and measurement bias. The governing three-coupling is infrared thermal imaging x physiological regulation x heat-transfer models. The research treats “external qi” as a cultural and experimental task label, not an established physical energy carrier. The scientific core separates raw infrared radiance from inferred skin temperature and estimated heat flux. It develops emissivity and reflected-wall correction, blackbody calibration, spectral detector response, conduction and perfusion bioheat models, convection, evaporation, respiration-related temperature patterns, posture and muscular activity. The original candidate bulk heat equation is explicitly refined by separating volumetric tissue transport from surface heat-transfer boundary conditions. The principal proposed test uses concealed task assignments, matched breathing/movement/clothing, phantom references, negative-control regions and conventional physics-first rivals. Thirty physically distinct mathematical plates document governing relationships, units, assumptions, identifiability, masked falsifiers and chapter links. Eighty-two independent research chapters contain 410 single-page investigations. The true center of the monograph is its 200 one-page Research Gates, each posing a falsifiable question in bold deep-navy typography and asking what an independent successor must measure, challenge, disprove or preserve. Thirty-three differentiated Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future instruments, error-correction artifacts, negative-result protocols and reproducibility tools. The DOI registry separates three STARLI author mother volumes from eleven externally published methodological or conventional-science references on infrared thermography, emissivity, classical bioheat and research design. Bibliographic sources constrain methods; they do not validate extraordinary qigong mechanisms. Every integrated experiment is prospective. The book presents no completed human intervention, clinically established effect, new physical particle or evidence of treatment efficacy. Ethical authorization and independent scientific review would be required before future human-observation research. items.summary: Computational research data accompanying the manuscript State Ordering and Spatial Cancellation in Helicene Chiroptical Response: Analysis with ChiroptMap , by Yuuya Nagata and Takashi Hirose. The archive contains native quantum-chemical inputs and outputs, wavefunctions and transition amplitudes, numerical field-analysis results, derived tables and deterministic reproduction code. 27 quantum-calculation records: ten exact-C2 interpolation scan points, four CAM-TDA controls, four Gaussian full-response endpoints, four unconstrained excited-state geometry candidates, two ground-state geometries, and three M3-M5 TDA benchmarks. Four fixed-core composition/geometry controls, including parent outputs, complete TDA amplitude JSON, WFX files, optimization trajectories and inputs. 22 full-grid state-field results: 16 control conditions and six M3-M5 conditions; two additional full-grid M5/S2 refinements at h=0.1 and 0.05 bohr; and independent separable quadrature/localization diagnostics. Eight S1 reference-field conditions and sixteen independent post-processing convergence controls, with source inputs and numerical settings. Five-molecule benchmark inputs and native Gaussian outputs, formatted checkpoints, ORCA data, validation fields, and benchmark tables. Unrounded state, origin, partition, relaxation and method tables; atom-to-region definitions; frozen numerical implementations; and relative-path parameter records. The ZIP contains 911 files (1,810,549,238 compressed bytes). DATA_DICTIONARY.txt describes the directory structure, units and interpretation. MANIFEST.csv records payload paths, byte counts and SHA-256 hashes. Complete ORCA amplitudes and occupied-orbital WFX files, Gaussian canonical-SCF all-orbital WFX files and native formatted checkpoints are included for the documented workflows. Gaussian and ORCA executables are not distributed. The M5/S2 h=0.05-bohr full-grid result meets the explicit electric-vector, magnetic-vector and C_R refinement targets documented in the data dictionary. Grid completion alone does not establish numerical convergence or state identity. Separable linear diagnostics are distinct from full-grid field calculations; native C1 labels are not exact C2 irreducible representations. No frequency-certified minimum or S2-emission assignment is implied by an electronically converged geometry calculation. Frozen code snapshots preserve the calculations as run. The separately archived ChiroptMap v0.3.0 software record (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23644576) provides the installable analysis methods; the v0.2.0 core source archive (doi:10.5281/zenodo.22168280) documents the inherited direct-workflow implementation. Relative parameter records allow numerical reruns without access to the original execution host. Full-grid regeneration may require substantial computing resources. Research data are released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Included software retains its original MIT licenses.

items.summary: Supervised pairwise graph representations convert pairwise predictive relations into sample-specific graphs, but graph-level accuracy does not by itself show that higher-order topology carries the signal. In a controlled Transformer error-detection task, supervised pairwise graphs outperform attention-as-adjacency (ROC-AUC $0.839$ versus $0.559$; the comparable no-confidence pair is $0.687$ versus $0.559$), but their apparent advantage over model confidence disappears after controlling for sequence length, which is almost perfectly recoverable from the pooled hidden state ($R^2=0.9995$). On published HCP Emotion ensemble graphs, signed node aggregation already acts as an ensemble of supervised pairwise predictions. Edge magnitude alone is near chance; topology-aware augmentations change ROC-AUC by at most $0.004$, with only sign-separated degree showing small positive changes across all tested graph sizes, while a validation-tuned three-layer GCN provides no measurable improvement over the signed node-summary baseline. A Fisher post-hoc corrector satisfies its distribution-agnostic guarantees across the evaluated feature representations and remains stable under reduced labelled budgets; in a near-error-free fMRI calibration regime the bound correctly becomes statistically uninformative. A separate cross-attention analysis identifies a redundant reversal circuit and downstream EOS-timing and copy failures. Higher-order topology should therefore be credited only after local supervised evidence and recoverable nuisance variables have been excluded.
items.title: Interpreting Supervised Pairwise Graph Representations: Local Evidence, Confounding, and Provable Post-hoc Correction

items.summary: Training large language models (LLMs) in sub-8-bit arithmetic promises substantial gains in memory bandwidth and compute throughput, yet FP4 formats introduce quantization error severe enough to destabilize optimization if left unaddressed. We present ALTO, an open-source training recipe for GPT-OSS-20B, a 20-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, on the MLPerf Small MoE Training benchmark under the MXFP4 microscaling format. The recipe combines established techniques from Abecassis, Felix et al. [arXiv:2509.25149] (hybrid 1D/2D block quantization, randomized Hadamard transforms, and stochastic rounding) with a simplified weight de-oscillation scheme adapted from TetraJet-v2 [arXiv:2510.27527]. On C4 validation at global batch size 16, MXFP4 + RHT + SR + de-oscillation reaches a validation loss of 3.3350 at 16,128 steps, only 0.007 above the BF16 baseline (3.3283), closing roughly 50% of the gap left by MXFP4 without de-oscillation (3.3418). Measured by steps to reach the MLPerf quality target (validation loss 3.34), de-oscillation cuts the FP4 convergence overhead relative to BF16 from +20.0% to +5.0%. We also report negative end-to-end results from differential gradient estimation, outlier clipping, and macro-block scaling, despite each showing operator-level SNR gains. All experiments use simulated MXFP4 kernels on AMD MI300 hardware and wall-clock speed has not been optimized.
items.title: Training an MoE LLM in MXFP4: How We Closed the Gap to BF16

items.summary: Scenario-Robust Coordinated Beamforming for Cell-Free ISAC under Imperfect CSI This repository contains the full simulator, notebooks, configuration files, and result checkpoints for the paper “Scenario-Robust Coordinated Beamforming for Cell-Free ISAC under Imperfect CSI: Outage Control and Sensing-Information Preservation.” The method, SR-CBSA, is a scenario-robust coordinated block successive convex approximation scheme for joint communication and sensing beamforming in distributed cell-free massive MIMO ISAC networks under pilot-based CSI uncertainty. It enforces direct global received-signal SINR constraints over sampled channel-error scenarios, preserves target-directed sensing power and a transmit-side azimuth-information surrogate, and stabilizes sequential per-access-point updates through trust regions, damping, proximal regularization, and penalized feasibility slack. Training, held-out validation, the physical true channel, and unseen-error test scenarios are kept strictly separate, so the reported gains reflect genuine robustness rather than overfitting to the sampled errors. The code reproduces every result in the paper from seed-controlled experiments: the paired Monte Carlo study across 5, 10, 15, and 20 dB pilot SNR, the same-realization method comparison, the QoS-target feasibility sweep, the responsibility-rule ablation, the scenario-count and synchronization-error sensitivity studies, the full-rank and locally low-rank scalability cases, and the baseline comparisons including the adapted JointOpt framework and a feasible max-min robust SOCP relaxation. All optimization uses CVXPY with CLARABEL, runs on CPU, and writes CSV checkpoints so long runs can be resumed and verified independently. Set the experiment flags in the configuration cell, run the notebook top to bottom, and the module and figures are regenerated automatically. See the README for environment setup, the flag-to-experiment mapping, and the fixed seeds used for each reported table and figure.
items.title: Scenario-Robust Coordinated Beamforming for Cell-Free ISAC under Imperfect CSI: Outage Control and Sensing-Information Preservation
